building_description.value: Small one-story, one-room chapel, three bays wide by three bays deep, with narrow apse extension and central belfry tower. Main building completed 1887; belfry tower added 1894. Wood frame structural system clad with drop siding; red brick pier foundation infilled with matching brick. Front-gabled roof covered with tin shingles. Contributing resource to Magruder Village Historic District (DHR ID#099-5240).
building_description.quote: The church building is a small, one-story, one-room chapel. It is three bays-wide by three bays deep, and has a narrow apse extension from the rear (south), as well as a central belfry tower projecting from the front (north). The main building was completed in 1887, and subsequently was expanded with the front belfry tower in 1894. The main block has a wood frame structural system clad with drop siding and beaded corner boards. It rests on a red brick pier foundation that has been infilled with matching brick

sheets.title: PLUMBING FLOOR PLANS — REHABILITATION
sheets.source_pdf: 20-091.2022.10.07.FINAL ALL DRAWINGS CLIN 0002.pdf (page 1); also in 10/14/22 revision
sheets.reading_notes: Shows two floor plans: demolition plan (remove all plumbing fixtures; waste piping and domestic cold water to remain for reuse) and new construction plan. New work: flush tank water closet connecting to existing piping; wall-hung lavatory connecting to existing piping. CW (cold water) piping runs from crawl space at 3/4-inch and 1/2-inch. Exterior yard hydrant noted as existing. Handhole with frozen shut-off valve to be replaced. Building has no hot water heating equipment — domestic cold water service only (general note). Very small footprint: plumbing serves a single restroom alcove. Layout confirms single-story, small-to-modest footprint building.

sheets.title: MECHANICAL FLOOR PLANS — REHABILITATION
sheets.reading_notes: Shows demolition and new work plans for HVAC. Existing: electric baseboard heaters (BBH) throughout main chapel and alcoves — ~10 units visible on demolition plan. New: replacement electric baseboard heaters (BB-1 through BB-10 per M-701 schedule) plus one fin tube heater; thermostats replaced with new 7-day programmable type. Heating is entirely electric resistance. No cooling system shown or noted — building is heating-only. Controls: refer to M-701.

sheets.title: SCHEDULE AND CONTROLS
sheets.source_pdf: 20-091.2022.10.07.FINAL ALL DRAWINGS CLIN 0002.pdf (page 3); also in 10/14/22 revision
sheets.reading_notes: Baseboard unit heater schedule: BB-1 through BB-10, all floor-mounted. Capacities range from 396 to 2900 BTUH. Electric service: 120V, 375W to 1000W. HVAC design conditions: indoor winter 65°F, summer 50% RH; outdoor summer 91°F db / 77°F MWB, winter 17°F. Controls points list: zone temperature (AI, alarm, trend, show on graphic), heating stage 1 (BO), heating setpoint (alarm, trend, show on graphic), schedule (software loop), low zone setpoint (AI, alarm). Fin tube heater sequence of operation: occupied mode 70°F setpoint, unoccupied 65°F night setback. One-stage electric heating control. Note: no cooling or ventilation controls shown — building is electric heat only.

sheets.title: LEGEND, ABBREVIATIONS AND SCHEDULE
sheets.source_pdf: 20-091.2022.10.07.FINAL ALL DRAWINGS CLIN 0002.pdf (page 4); also in 10/14/22 revision
sheets.reading_notes: Electrical legend, abbreviations, and panelboard schedule. Existing Panelboard 'A' Schedule: 125A, MLO, 240V/120V, 1-phase, 3-wire, 10 kAIC min, surface mount. Loads: baseboard heater circuits, parking lot lighting (20A 120V), receptacles (interior & exterior), GFCI receptacles/flood lights. GE load center (Type 1, TLMG125 MOD). Fed from 2-pole 100A NEMA 3R disconnect switch on exterior of building. Note: drawings were PE-stamped by Richard K. Huang, EE, Virginia. Arc Flash warning label included (UFC 3-560-01). All existing electrical equipment, lighting, and devices must have new wiring — full rewire scope.

sheets.title: ELECTRICAL SITE PLAN — REHABILITATION
sheets.reading_notes: Electrical site plan showing Building 2707 in context of its cemetery/site setting. Shows existing panelboard 'A' location on building exterior; parking lot lighting run (direct buried schedule 40 PVC conduit, min 24 inches deep); area/street lighting on 14' poles per fixture schedule E-501 (not in this drawing set). Site shows burial plots, headstones, mature trees (48-inch oak, 12-inch cedar, 6-inch dogwood), wood picket fence, brick wall, chain rail barrier. Gravel parking area; gas valve and swale at site perimeter. Note: rehabilitation includes new parking lot lighting fed from spare circuit breaker in panel 'A'. Site plan confirms small, rural/wooded setting on active DoD installation.

sheets.title: FLOOR PLAN — DEMOLITION (ELECTRICAL)
sheets.reading_notes: Electrical demolition floor plan. Scope includes full rewire: disconnect/remove existing baseboard heater wiring (reconnect circuit to new baseboard heater with new wiring); disconnect existing outdoor flood lights and remove all wiring; existing panelboard 'A' to remain; existing ground cover 'KRALDY 6X6 COVER' to remain; save and reinstall existing exterior weatherproof GFCI receptacles and disconnect switch; save and reinstall incandescent pendant light fixtures (above entry door) and wall-mounted incandescent light fixtures. Confirms: all existing electrical devices and wiring must be replaced/renewed — this is a full electrical rehabilitation. Single floor plan layout confirms small 1-story building with main chapel space plus side alcove/toilet room plus entry vestibule.
